Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **147** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2b1382a5b3887e4abd194411ef77a7cd368c95c2` → `packageMentionDocs`.

git fetch origin 9768300ae6e33c58cbeda2f8373964c66ff726d9 && git checkout 9768300ae6e33c58cbeda2f8373964c66ff726d9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2b1382a5b3887e4abd194411ef77a7cd368c95c2 df6803d15923a60a4dc32700d36b563f1b30a4e9 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2b1382a5b3887e4abd194411ef77a7cd368c95c2 && git merge --no-ff df6803d15923a60a4dc32700d36b563f1b30a4e9

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than

> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2b1382a5b3887e4abd194411ef77a7cd368c95c2` → pass the list as

### ① Derived judgments

**1. `TursoConfigSchema`'s accept set and its reach into `DatasourceSchema` — RIGHT for every local and replica shape; WRONG for one local-file shape (FAIL item 1 below).** The new arm in `tursoTransportIssues` sits inside the `mode !== 'remote'` branch, after the url, in-memory-replica, forced-replica and forced-local refusals, and refuses a `typeof string && length greater than 0` key on `encryptionKey` with one text per mode (`${arm}` is the only interpolation). It reaches `DatasourceSchema` through `reportDriverConfigIssues` (re-pathed `config.encryptionKey`), `validateDriverConfig` (`config-registry.zod.ts:596`), hence `defineStack` / `os validate`, and the admin save door (`assertValidConfig` at `datasource-admin-service.ts:1031`, plus `recordRefusal`, which parses the whole `DatasourceSchema`). An empty key is accepted (unset, as `buildTursoDriverConfig` reads it); a lone `sync` stays the refinement's first issue with this one second — all of it pinned in `packages/spec/src/data/driver/turso.test.ts` (ten refused shapes across two modes, order rows, both doors, controls, no-echo, the describe). The hole: `tursoTransportModeOf` returns a FORCED mode first, and the `mode === 'remote'` branch judges only `timeoutMs` and `syncUrl` — so `{ url: 'file:./data/app.db', mode: 'remote', encryptionKey: KEY }` parses at every authoring door.

**2. `TursoDriver`'s constructor accept set — RIGHT for every local and replica shape; WRONG for the same shape.** `if (mode !== 'remote' && config.encryptionKey) refuseIgnoredSyncKey(localEncryptionKeyRefusal(mode))` is raised before `super()`, after the four sync-key refusals and the `localEngineDefect` / timeout refusals, so each config keeps the refusal that names its way out; `createTursoDriver` is `new TursoDriver` (`index.ts:97`); both loaders — `runtime/turso-driver-factory.ts:288` and `default-datasource-driver-factory.ts:1337` — and the CLI (`storage-driver.ts` loads the runtime factory) reach it through `buildTursoDriverConfig`. Pinned in the new refusal file: `file:`, `FILE:`, forced `local`, `:memory:`, `createTursoDriver`, and three replica shapes (driver-built client, supplied client, forced `replica`), each asserting `code`, `status`, the mode's first sentence and that no file exists afterwards; three controls round-trip a row and read the file back as `SQLite format 3`. The hole is the same guard: `detectMode` returns `config.mode` first, so a forced `remote` skips every local-engine refusal, this one included.

**3. The mirror's byte-equality — RIGHT.** Measured on the two head files: the `tursoTransportIssues` bodies differ only by two pre-existing mirror comments ("Unreachable through this mirror…", not this PR's); the `encryptionKey` arm and both describe strings are byte-identical. The parity table adds 8 key rows, 6 order rows and 2 empty-key accept rows, extends `SYNC_KEY_REFUSALS` to the new key, floors the local and replica halves apart (8 and 3) and the copied-message set at 31, and `driverConfigOf` drops an empty key the way the loaders do.

**4. `connect()`'s replica arm no longer forwarding the key — RIGHT.** After the constructor refusal a non-empty key cannot reach that `createClient`, and an empty one was already unset by the loaders; a forwarded key there would have been dead code that reads as a capability. `createRemoteClient` never forwarded it, before or after — which is what makes door 6 below a door.

**5. The ADR-0087 semantic entry — RIGHT.** `18.turso-config-local-encryption-key-refused.ts` carries `id`, `surface`, `replacement`, `reason`, `acceptanceCriteria`; its file name is the `major.id` shard the registry builder derives (`shardNameFor`); no `conversionIds`, correctly — a refusal judges no mechanical D2 edit, and `migrations.test.ts` would refuse a fabricated one; no `relevantWhen`, so it is always listed (the conservative choice for a surface under `datasources[].config`); `surface` carries no backtick, as the upgrade-guide renderer needs. The changeset's adr-0087 marker names it `registered`, and `check:spec-changes` / `check:upgrade-guide` ran inside the green `Lint & Repo Gates` and `Type Check · source gates`. One nit, not blocking: `reason` names `OS_ALLOW_DRIVER_CONNECT_FAILURE`, the escape hatch `connect-failure-remedy.ts` deliberately never names even to warn against; an upgrade TODO that hands an upgrading agent the hatch is the opposite of that design — drop the clause.

**6. The redaction comment — RIGHT, and incomplete.** `STILL_WRITABLE_CREDENTIAL_KEYS` has exactly one consumer, `redactableConfigKeys` (`datasource-credential-redaction.ts:383`); a remote turso row still parses with the key and a stored local row may still carry one, so the key must stay on the list and stay redacted on read — the rewritten comment at lines 126–133 says so correctly. The module header at lines 58–62 was not rewritten and still says the key is "an AES-256 key … injected at connect", which is now false for every local and replica row (flag 8 in ③).

**7. The five security answers.**

- **(a) Doors — one still writes plaintext.** ✔ `new TursoDriver` / `createTursoDriver`: a non-empty key on `file:` (any case, whitespace), `:memory:`, forced `local`, and on a replica (`file:` + `syncUrl`, supplied or driver-built client, forced `replica`) is refused before `super()`; no file is opened (pinned). ✔ Boot from `defineStack`: refused at parse (`DatasourceSchema`), and a config that reaches the loaders is refused at construction. ✔ A stored row: not re-parsed on load (no D2 conversion exists, by design); both loaders forward the key through `buildTursoDriverConfig` and the constructor refuses it — see (e). ✔ Admin save: `assertValidConfig` → issue at `config.encryptionKey`; `recordRefusal` parses the whole record. ✔ Admin test connection: `probe` → `factory.create` throws → `ok: false, "Failed to build driver: …"`; `connect()` is never reached. ✔ The CLI: `storage-driver.ts` resolves a turso definition from `OS_DATABASE_URL` / `OS_DATABASE_AUTH_TOKEN` (no key source) and loads the runtime host loader, the same constructor. ✔ libSQL client builders: the only two `createClient` sites on the head are in `turso-driver.ts`; the replica one is unreachable with a non-empty key and no longer forwards it; the Knex handle is built by `toKnexConfig` alone and carries no key. ✔ No example, skill, CLI scaffold, `create-objectstack` template or environment variable authors the key (grep on the head). **✗ Door 6 — a `file:` url under a forced `mode: 'remote'` with a non-empty key: `{ url: 'file:./data/app.db', mode: 'remote', encryptionKey: KEY }` parses at every authoring door (judgment 1), constructs (judgment 2: `toKnexConfig`'s remote arm opens nothing), and on `connect()` takes the remote arm: `createRemoteClient()` calls `createClient({ url, authToken, concurrency })` with the key dropped, and `@libsql/client` opens the local file for a `file:` url — the driver's own reading of `@libsql/core@0.18.0` in the `startsWithScheme` docblock, the row `file: under a forced mode: 'remote' … ctor: 'accept'` in the parity table (line 119) and the classification pin in `turso-driver-unrecognised-url-refusal.test.ts:303` all treat that shape as a supported one. Every read and write then runs through `RemoteTransport` over that file: a local database file written in plaintext under a declared key, the card's defect exactly, with the key silently dropped — the outcome the card's Expected forbids. The claim's carve-out ("the remote (`libsql://`) mode, whose encryption is the server's") does not cover it: there is no server and no `libsql://` url. No row in either test matrix carries a key under a forced `remote`, so no pin on this head exercises it. The `:memory:` variant of the same shape is accepted-and-dropped the same way and writes nothing to disk.** This is FAIL item 1.
- **(b) Strip, coerce or ignore — none on the local and replica paths; one on door 6.** `buildTursoDriverConfig`'s reader keeps a non-empty string key unchanged and drops only an empty or non-string one (truthiness), which matches the spec's `length greater than 0` and the constructor's truthiness test (a whitespace-only key is refused by both; a non-string is a type issue at the spec and truthy at the constructor). No `??` fallback, no coercion, no normalisation before the arm. The one strip-and-continue is `createRemoteClient` ignoring the key under door 6.
- **(c) No echo — RIGHT.** Both builders (`localEncryptionKeyRefusal` in the driver, the arm in both schemas) interpolate `${arm}` only: no url, no key, no issue id; `refuseIgnoredSyncKey`'s header says the same of the family. The url refusals a key-bearing config meets first (order rows) echo only the scheme and the forced mode, never the url or the key. Pinned twice: spec `never echoes the key or either url`, driver `the message names no url and no key`.
- **(d) Envelope — RIGHT.** `refuseIgnoredSyncKey` sets `code = StandardErrorCode.enum.VALIDATION_ERROR` and `status = 400`, the ADR-0112 shape; every constructor pin asserts both `code` and `status`. The authoring side is a zod `custom` issue on `['encryptionKey']`, re-pathed `config.encryptionKey` under `DatasourceSchema`, which the admin door surfaces as `Invalid configuration for driver 'turso'. config.encryptionKey: …`; the spec pins assert path and message.
- **(e) A stored row fails closed — RIGHT.** `factory.create` throws; `datasource-connection-service.ts` records `failed-degraded` with `datasource 'NAME': connect failed — MESSAGE` (lines 387, 489, 732, 986); under ADR-0062 D5 it throws fail-fast when objects bind or route to the datasource or it is boot-critical, unless `OS_ALLOW_DRIVER_CONNECT_FAILURE` is set, and otherwise warns and leaves it unconnected with state `error` in Setup → Datasources; a test connection answers `ok: false`. The row is never connected with the key dropped. (A row no object addresses is skipped by the D2 gate and never connected either — pre-existing, and not this defect.)

### ② Semver level

RIGHT. The changeset grades `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/driver-turso` `minor`, BREAKING, with the FROM → TO table and the one-line fix; the title carries `!`; the PR body and the changeset both carry `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. That is what the diff publishes: the accept set of `TursoConfigSchema` (through `DatasourceSchema`), of the mirror and of `new TursoDriver()` narrows — a config that parsed and constructed is refused — and no key, export or symbol is added, removed or renamed (`TursoTransportIssue.path` and `TursoTransportKeys` are module-local; the schema shape is unchanged; the describe change regenerated `content/docs/references/data/driver-turso.mdx`, the one stale artifact). BREAKING-as-minor is the amended ruling the triage cites and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` enforces; `Check Changeset` is green. The ADR-0087 disposition marker is present and names the registered entry. `@objectstack/service-datasource` changes no behaviour (a stale TSDoc only, flag 7) and owes no changeset. The FAIL item does not move the level: its fix is one more narrowing of the same face.

### ③ Boundary flags

**FAIL item 1 (door 6, ① 7(a)).** A `file:` url (or `:memory:`) under a forced `mode: 'remote'` with a non-empty `encryptionKey` is accepted at every authoring door and at construction, and `connect()` opens the local file through the native libSQL client with the key dropped: plaintext under a declared key. Fix in this PR, narrowly, so the claim's scope holds: decide the key refusal by where the file lives, not by the mode — in the spec's `mode === 'remote'` branch (and the mirror, byte for byte) an arm for a `file:` / `:memory:` url beside a non-empty key, and in the constructor the same predicate independent of `mode` — with its own text (in this mode the engine is the client the driver builds, which is handed no key), parity rows for `file:` and `:memory:` under a forced `remote` with a key (refused on `encryptionKey`), a constructor pin asserting no file exists, and the dev's ablation leg over the new arm. Route B (refuse the key in every mode) also closes it, but then the placeholder-family row and the redaction suites that author the key on `libsql://` urls lose their home, and the claim's remote carve-out is overridden — declare it as a deviation if chosen.

**The open question — remote mode after this PR.** (i) Leaving the `libsql://` remote mode accepting-and-dropping the key does NOT block this PR: the claim put that mode out of scope in writing, the card's measurement and title are the local file, and on a true remote url nothing is written in plaintext by this driver (the server's storage is the server's). It is a correct follow-up — but only for `libsql://` / `https://` / `ws(s)://` urls; a local url under a forced remote mode is inside the card (FAIL item 1). (ii) Recommended route: **A — retire the key with a tombstone**, as the follow-up card, through the `spec-property-retirement` kit. Why: measured on this head, zero producers author it; a key the runtime honours in no mode is the ADR-0049 removal case, and `retiredKey()` carries the prescription in every mode and on every door at once, keeping the liveness-ledger row; B leaves a published slot whose only purpose is to be refused — a key every AI author will still write — and makes the `STILL_WRITABLE_CREDENTIAL_KEYS` comment, the placeholder-family row and the redaction fixtures describe a value that parses nowhere; C leaves the accepted-and-dropped shape the card forbids on the one mode where it still exists. The retirement's cost (a dozen surfaces, fixtures re-homed, `STILL_WRITABLE_CREDENTIAL_KEYS` losing its only member) is the kit's ordinary cost, and it is the same work B would only defer.

**Dev deviations, each answered.** 1. File surface widened to the producer (`packages/spec` arm, test, ADR-0087 entry, redaction comment, placeholder fixture, docs): correct — the dispatch allowed it, and the parity test holds authoring equal to construction, so a constructor-only refusal would have reopened that class. 2. `@objectstack/spec` graded `minor` beside `driver-turso`: correct, the published schema narrows. 3. The replica arm no longer forwards the key: correct (① 4). 4. Replica with a key against a reachable sync server NOT MEASURED: accepted — the refusal fires at construction before any client exists, and the pin asserts no file; nothing this PR claims depends on it. 5. Six gates re-run at the same head after a full build: accepted; the head's check-runs are the gate verdicts here. 6. Model-free commit trailers and the session-URL body footer: the repo's own form; accepted.

**Out-of-scope finding (remote mode accepts and drops the key; `@libsql/client`'s remote client would refuse it with `ENCRYPTION_KEY_NOT_SUPPORTED`):** class b, reach measured by the dev; escalated above as the follow-up (route A). It is not filed by this record: the seat routes it with the card's route choice.

**Further findings, non-blocking, fix in this PR with item 1.** 7. `packages/services/service-datasource/src/turso-driver-config.ts:66` — `TursoDriverConfigInput.encryptionKey`, a public export of `@objectstack/service-datasource` (`index.ts:149`), still reads "AES-256 key for the local database file (local/replica modes)": the one promise the text sweep missed. 8. `packages/spec/src/data/datasource-credential-redaction.ts:58-62` — the module header still says the key "stays injected at connect"; rewrite to match the table comment below it. 9. ① 5's nit on `OS_ALLOW_DRIVER_CONNECT_FAILURE` in the entry's `reason`. 10. Pre-existing, noted only: the mirror declares no `mode`, so forced-mode rows skip the mirror by design (parity header), and the only bytes by which the two `tursoTransportIssues` bodies differ are two mirror-side comments — neither is this PR's to change.
